newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila overnight money holds in liquid market.
newsitem.headline: Manila overnight money holds in liquid market.

text.p: * Volume rises to 19.714 bln from 17.538 bln pesos
Manila overnight money stayed firm at an average of 9.9375 percent on Monday even after substantial cash was drained by the Central Bank's dollar sales last week, dealers said.
The Central Bank sold over $100 million last week in order to curb the peso's weakness. This eventually soaked up some of banks' peso liquidity.
"The market is so liquid. It easily adjusted," a foreign bank dealer said.
Rates were in a tight band from 10.15625 to 9.9375 percent. A total of 57 financial institutions participated, of which 37 were lenders.
The secondary market was marked by a lot of sellers because banks think T-bill rates would now start to move up after weeks of decline, dealers said.
Late last week, the Central Bank gave a signal to the market that it did not want rates to move lower when it offered six-month reverse repos at a higher-than-market rate of 10.125.
"Banks would rather wait for the auction and buy there," a dealer said.
The weekly T-bill auction is scheduled later today and traders predict the rates in all maturities will move up a little.
A Reuter poll of six financial institutions gave secondary market offer rates of 9.425 to 9.575 percent for the three-month bills.
